adapt.simple: To change the way you do something so it works better in a new situation.
adapt.detailed: Living things and people adapt when they alter habits, tools, or features to suit a new habitat, climate, or problem.
adapt.zh: 适应；调整自身以适合新环境
adapt.example: Desert plants adapt to dry soil by storing water in thick leaves.
adapt.basic: The plants change so they can live there.

adjust.simple: To make a small change so something fits, works, or reads correctly.
adjust.detailed: You adjust a setting, measurement, or plan by shifting it slightly until the result is accurate or comfortable.
adjust.zh: 调节；微调使合适或准确
adjust.example: We adjust the microscope so the pond-water cells come into clear focus.
adjust.basic: We move the knob a little so we can see.

apply.simple: To use a skill, rule, or idea in a real task or new problem.
apply.detailed: Students apply knowledge when they take what they have learnt and use it to solve a question, write a text, or complete a practical job.
apply.zh: 应用；把知识或规则用到实际问题上
apply.example: On the scholarship paper, apply the same fraction rule to every worded problem.
apply.basic: Use what you learnt on the new questions.

argue.simple: To give reasons that support a point of view in a careful way.
argue.detailed: In academic writing, you argue when you state a claim and back it with evidence, not when you just shout or disagree.
argue.zh: 论证；提出理由来支持一种看法
argue.example: In the waste debate, argue that the canteen should stop selling single-use bottles.
argue.basic: Say what you think and why.

arrange.simple: To put things in a clear order or to plan how they will happen.
arrange.detailed: You arrange objects, ideas, or events so they follow a useful sequence, grouping, or timetable.
arrange.zh: 安排；整理成有序的样子
arrange.example: Arrange your research notes under headings before you write the inquiry report.
arrange.basic: Put the notes in a tidy order.

assemble.simple: To put separate parts together so they make a whole.
assemble.detailed: In science and design, you assemble equipment or a model by joining pieces in the correct order so the system can work.
assemble.zh: 组装；把零部件拼成整体
assemble.example: Assemble the circuit in the order shown before you test the bulb.

calculate.simple: To work out a number by using maths, not by guessing.
calculate.detailed: You calculate when you use an operation, formula, or measured values to find an exact or estimated numerical answer.
calculate.example: Calculate the average height of the bean plants after two weeks.
calculate.basic: Work out the number with maths.

categorise.simple: To sort things into groups that share the same kind of feature.
categorise.detailed: You categorise information when you place items into named groups so patterns are easier to compare and explain.
categorise.zh: 归类；按共同特征分成类别
categorise.example: Categorise the library books as fiction, information, or poetry before shelving them.

challenge.simple: To question an idea and ask for stronger reasons or evidence.
challenge.detailed: You challenge a claim when you test it, point out a weakness, or ask whether the proof is good enough.
challenge.zh: 质疑；对观点提出异议并要求更好的理由
challenge.example: Challenge the claim that plastic bags are harmless if the article gives no data.
challenge.basic: Ask if that opinion is really true.

clarify.simple: To make an idea clearer so other people can understand it.
clarify.detailed: You clarify writing or speech by adding detail, defining a word, or removing anything that confuses the reader.
clarify.example: Clarify the last sentence so the marker knows which creek site you measured.
clarify.basic: Make the sentence easier to understand.

classify.simple: To sort living things or objects into scientific groups.
classify.detailed: Scientists classify organisms or materials by shared features so they can be named, compared, and studied in an organised way.
classify.zh: 分类；按科学标准划分种类
classify.example: Classify the creek animals as insects, fish, or crustaceans using the identification key.

collect.simple: To bring things together so you can use or study them.
collect.detailed: You collect samples, data, or objects by gathering them carefully, often following a method so the set is useful.
collect.zh: 收集；把东西或数据聚集起来
collect.example: Collect water samples from three points along the creek after the rain.
collect.basic: Pick up the things you need.

combine.simple: To join two or more things so they work or appear as one.
combine.detailed: You combine materials, ideas, or results when you put them together to make a mixture, a stronger point, or a new whole.
combine.zh: 结合；把几样东西合在一起
combine.example: Combine the two data tables so the class can compare morning and afternoon temperatures.

communicate.simple: To share information, ideas, or feelings so others understand.
communicate.detailed: You communicate when you speak, write, draw, or signal clearly enough that another person can follow your meaning.
communicate.zh: 交流；把信息或想法清楚地传达给别人
communicate.example: Communicate your findings in a short talk so Year 5 can follow the method.
communicate.basic: Tell people what you found out.

compose.simple: To create a piece of writing, music, or art with care.
compose.detailed: You compose when you invent and shape sentences, a poem, or a tune so the parts fit together as a finished work.
compose.zh: 创作；写出或谱出完整作品
compose.example: Compose a camp narrative that shows, rather than tells, how the storm began.

confirm.simple: To check that something is true or that a result is reliable.
confirm.detailed: You confirm a finding when a second test, source, or measurement matches the first one and removes doubt.
confirm.zh: 确认；核实某事属实或结果可靠
confirm.example: Confirm the pH reading by testing the same creek sample a second time.
confirm.basic: Check that the answer is right.

connect.simple: To join ideas, people, or things so they link together.
connect.detailed: You connect when you show a relationship between facts, or when you physically join parts so they work as a system.
connect.zh: 连接；把事物或想法联系起来
connect.example: Connect each heading in your plan to a piece of evidence from the article.
connect.basic: Show how the ideas go together.

construct.simple: To build something carefully, such as a model, sentence, or argument.
construct.detailed: You construct when you put parts together in a planned way so the finished object or piece of writing is solid and clear.
construct.zh: 构建；有计划地建造或组织起来
construct.example: Construct an argument with a claim, two reasons, and a short conclusion.
construct.basic: Build your answer step by step.

consult.simple: To ask a person or check a trusted source before you decide.
consult.detailed: You consult when you seek advice or information from an expert, elder, map, or document so your decision is better informed.
consult.zh: 咨询；向人或可靠资料请教后再决定
consult.example: Consult the 1901 Federation timeline before you date the photograph.
consult.basic: Look it up before you decide.

convert.simple: To change something from one form, unit, or use into another.
convert.detailed: You convert when you turn energy, units, materials, or ideas into a different but related form without losing the core amount or meaning.
convert.zh: 转换；把一种形式或单位变成另一种
convert.example: Convert the creek depth from centimetres to metres before you graph it.
convert.basic: Change the number into another unit.

convey.simple: To get a feeling, idea, or message across to the reader.
convey.detailed: Writers convey meaning through word choice, imagery, and tone so the audience understands more than the bare facts.
convey.zh: 传达；把情感或意思传递给读者
convey.example: The camp narrative should convey how tense the bush track felt after dusk.
convey.basic: Show the reader how it felt.

criticise.simple: To point out weaknesses in an idea, using reasons rather than insults.
criticise.detailed: You criticise a text or plan when you judge its faults fairly and explain what should be stronger or clearer.
criticise.zh: 批评；有根据地指出缺点，而非辱骂
criticise.example: Criticise the poster if it uses slogans but gives no facts about recycling.
criticise.basic: Say what is weak about the idea.

debate.simple: To discuss opposite views in an organised way, using reasons.
debate.detailed: You debate when two or more sides present arguments, listen, and test which case is better supported.
debate.zh: 辩论；双方有条理地陈述对立观点
debate.example: Debate whether the school oval should be watered every day in a drought.
debate.basic: Talk about both sides of the idea.

defend.simple: To protect a claim or person by giving reasons or support.
defend.detailed: You defend a view when you show why it is fair or true, using evidence against criticism or attack.
defend.zh: 辩护；用理由或证据维护某种立场
defend.example: Defend your view on school uniforms with two facts, not only personal taste.
defend.basic: Stand up for your opinion with reasons.

describe.simple: To say what something is like using clear, specific details.
describe.detailed: You describe a person, place, or process by naming features a reader could picture or recognise, not by giving a vague label.
describe.zh: 描述；用具体细节说明某事物是什么样的
describe.example: Describe the billabong so a reader can picture the still water and paperbarks.

design.simple: To plan how something will look or work before you make it.
design.detailed: You design a product, test, or layout by choosing materials, steps, and features that fit a purpose.
design.zh: 设计；在动手前规划外观或工作方式
design.example: Design an experiment that fairly tests which soil holds the most water.
design.basic: Plan how the test will work.

develop.simple: To grow or improve an idea, skill, or piece of work over time.
develop.detailed: You develop writing or thinking when you add depth, fix weaknesses, and make the result more complete than the first attempt.
develop.zh: 发展；逐步完善想法、技能或作品
develop.example: Develop your first sentence into a full paragraph with a reason and an example.
develop.basic: Make the idea longer and better.

discuss.simple: To talk or write about a topic from more than one angle.
discuss.detailed: You discuss an issue when you examine reasons for and against, or several explanations, instead of giving only one short opinion.
discuss.zh: 讨论；从多个角度谈一个问题
discuss.example: Discuss both sides of the canteen menu change before you vote.

document.simple: To write down what happened so there is a clear record.
document.detailed: You document a test or observation by noting dates, methods, and results that another person could check later.
document.zh: 记录；把过程或结果写成可查的资料
document.example: Document every change you make to the model boat so the class can repeat the test.

draft.simple: To write a first version that you expect to improve later.
draft.detailed: You draft a story or essay when you get ideas onto the page in order, knowing you will revise wording and structure afterwards.
draft.zh: 起草；写出准备以后修改的初稿
draft.example: Draft the camp scene tonight, then tighten the verbs tomorrow.
draft.basic: Write the first version of the story.

edit.simple: To check and change writing so it is clearer, correct, and stronger.
edit.detailed: You edit when you fix grammar, cut extra words, and improve word choice after the ideas are already on the page.
edit.zh: 编辑；检查并修改文字使更清楚、正确
edit.example: Edit the camp narrative so every sentence earns its place.
edit.basic: Fix the writing and make it neater.

eliminate.simple: To remove something that is not needed or that causes a problem.
eliminate.detailed: You eliminate a variable, error, or option when you take it out so the remaining test or choice is fairer and clearer.
eliminate.zh: 排除；去掉不需要或会造成干扰的部分
eliminate.example: Eliminate draughts from the window so the candle test stays fair.
eliminate.basic: Take out the thing that spoils the test.

encourage.simple: To give someone support so they feel able to keep trying.
encourage.detailed: You encourage a person or group when your words or actions make them more confident, willing, or hopeful.
encourage.zh: 鼓励；给予支持使人更有信心继续努力
encourage.example: Local leaders encourage families to vote in the council election.
encourage.basic: Tell people they can keep going.

examine.simple: To look at something closely so you can understand it.
examine.detailed: You examine a text, object, or result when you study the details carefully instead of glancing and guessing.
examine.zh: 审视；仔细查看以便理解
examine.example: Examine the graph before you write which week the seedlings grew fastest.

expand.simple: To make an idea longer or wider by adding useful detail.
expand.detailed: You expand a sentence or plan when you add examples, reasons, or extra steps so the meaning is fuller, not just wordier.
expand.zh: 扩展；补充有用细节使内容更充分
expand.example: Expand your topic sentence with one fact from the Federation article.

explain.simple: To make something understandable by showing how or why it happens.
explain.detailed: You explain when you give causes, steps, or reasons that help another person follow an idea without guessing.
explain.zh: 解释；说明某事如何发生或为什么如此
explain.example: Explain why the ice melted faster on the black tray than on the white one.
explain.basic: Say how it works and why.

explore.simple: To look into a place, topic, or idea to find out more.
explore.detailed: You explore when you investigate with curiosity—walking a site, reading sources, or trying questions—before you decide what matters.
explore.zh: 探索；深入了解一个地方、主题或想法
explore.example: Explore the old maps to see how the harbour changed after Federation.
explore.basic: Look around and find out more.

express.simple: To show a thought or feeling in words, art, or action.
express.detailed: You express an idea when you choose language or images that let other people share what you mean or feel.
express.zh: 表达；用语言、艺术或行动说出想法或感受
express.example: Express the character’s fear through short sentences, not by naming the emotion.

extend.simple: To make something longer, wider, or more complete.
extend.detailed: You extend a line, deadline, or argument when you add length or reach so it covers more ground.
extend.zh: 延伸；使更长、更广或更完整
extend.example: Extend the number line past 100 so the class can plot the extra scores.

extract.simple: To take a needed part out of a larger whole.
extract.detailed: You extract a quote, sample, or substance when you pull the useful piece from a text, mixture, or site.
extract.zh: 提取；从整体中取出需要的部分
extract.example: Extract chlorophyll from the spinach leaves using the method in the lab sheet.

gather.simple: To bring people, facts, or objects together in one place.
gather.detailed: You gather information or materials when you collect them from different spots so you can use the set as a whole.
gather.zh: 收集；把人或资料聚到一起
gather.example: Gather leaf samples from both banks of the creek before you compare colour.

generate.simple: To make or produce something new, such as power, ideas, or heat.
generate.detailed: You generate a result when a process creates energy, data, or possibilities that were not there before.
generate.zh: 产生；制造出能量、想法或结果
generate.example: The small turbine can generate enough electricity to light one classroom lamp.

highlight.simple: To point out the most important part so it stands out.
highlight.detailed: You highlight a fact or phrase when you draw attention to it because it matters most for the task.
highlight.zh: 突出；标出最重要的部分
highlight.example: Highlight the command words on the scholarship paper before you start writing.

improve.simple: To make something better than it was before.
improve.detailed: You improve work when you change it so it is clearer, fairer, stronger, or more accurate.
improve.example: Improve the conclusion by naming the variable that actually changed the growth.

include.simple: To put something in as part of a group, list, or text.
include.detailed: You include a detail when you make sure it is present, not left out, because it belongs in the whole.
include.zh: 包括；把某部分放进整体之中
include.example: Include one quotation from the article in your inquiry paragraph.
include.basic: Put that part in as well.

inform.simple: To give someone facts they need to know.
inform.detailed: You inform an audience when you pass on accurate information so they can understand or decide.
inform.zh: 告知；把需要知道的事实告诉别人
inform.example: Inform the class about the excursion times in a short, factual notice.

inspect.simple: To look over something carefully to check its condition.
inspect.detailed: You inspect equipment, a site, or a sample when you check each part for safety, damage, or accuracy.
inspect.zh: 检查；仔细察看状态或是否合格
inspect.example: Inspect the beakers for cracks before you heat the water.
inspect.basic: Look over it to check it is safe.

instruct.simple: To tell someone clearly how to do a task.
instruct.detailed: You instruct when you give ordered steps or rules that another person can follow without guessing.
instruct.zh: 指导；清楚地告诉别人如何完成任务
instruct.example: Instruct the group to measure twice and record both readings.
instruct.basic: Tell them how to do the job.

introduce.simple: To bring a new person, idea, or topic in for the first time.
introduce.detailed: You introduce something when you present it so others know what it is and why it matters before you go deeper.
introduce.zh: 介绍；首次引出一个人、想法或主题
introduce.example: Introduce your main idea in the first sentence of the scholarship essay.
introduce.basic: Start by saying what the topic is.

invent.simple: To make a new thing or method that did not exist before.
invent.detailed: You invent when you design an original tool, story device, or solution rather than copying one that already exists.
invent.zh: 发明；创造出以前没有的东西或方法
invent.example: Invent a simple filter that can clean muddy water from the school tank.
invent.basic: Make up a new way to do it.

locate.simple: To find the exact place of a person, object, or site.
locate.detailed: You locate something when you work out where it is on a map, in a text, or in the real landscape.
locate.example: Locate the goldfield towns on the outline map of Victoria.

measure.simple: To find out the size, amount, or degree of something using units.
measure.detailed: You measure when you use a tool and a unit so a length, mass, time, or temperature can be compared fairly.
measure.zh: 测量；用单位求出大小、数量或程度
measure.example: Measure the creek width at the same rock each week.
measure.basic: Find out how big or how much it is.

modify.simple: To change part of something so it works better or fits a new need.
modify.detailed: You modify a design or method when you alter one feature on purpose, then check whether the result improves.
modify.zh: 修改；有针对地改动一部分使更合适
modify.example: Modify the paper-plane wing and test whether the flight lasts longer.
modify.basic: Change one part and try again.

monitor.simple: To watch something over time so you notice changes.
monitor.detailed: You monitor a system when you check it regularly and record what happens, rather than looking only once.
monitor.zh: 监测；持续观察以便发现变化
monitor.example: Monitor the tank level each morning during the dry spell.

participate.simple: To take part in an activity instead of only watching.
participate.detailed: You participate when you join a discussion, vote, game, or community event and contribute as a member.
participate.zh: 参与；加入活动而不是旁观
participate.example: Every student should participate in the class vote on the new playground rules.
participate.basic: Join in instead of sitting out.

perform.simple: To carry out a task, test, or action, often in front of others.
perform.detailed: You perform a procedure when you complete the steps correctly; you also perform when you present music or drama.
perform.zh: 进行；执行一项任务、实验或表演
perform.example: Perform the dissolving test three times so the class can trust the pattern.
perform.basic: Do the steps of the test.

persuade.simple: To get someone to agree by using reasons, not force.
persuade.detailed: You persuade an audience when your evidence and wording make them change or strengthen their view.
persuade.zh: 说服；用理由使人同意，而非强迫
persuade.example: Persuade the council that the creek path needs a bin at each bend.
persuade.basic: Try to get people to agree with you.

present.simple: To show information to an audience in a clear, organised way.
present.detailed: You present findings when you speak or display them so others can follow the method, results, and conclusion.
present.zh: 呈现；有条理地向听众展示信息
present.example: Present your inquiry findings in under three minutes, using one graph.
present.basic: Show the class what you found.

produce.simple: To make or create a result, object, or piece of work.
produce.detailed: A process produces an outcome when it generates a product, sound, gas, or finished text that can be observed.
produce.zh: 产生；制造出结果、物品或作品
produce.example: Green leaves produce oxygen during photosynthesis on a sunny day.
produce.basic: Make the thing that comes out at the end.

propose.simple: To put forward a plan or idea for other people to consider.
propose.detailed: You propose a solution when you offer it formally and invite others to accept, change, or reject it.
propose.zh: 提议；提出供他人考虑的计划或想法
propose.example: Propose a fair roster so every house team shares the oval after school.

prove.simple: To show that something is true using evidence that others can check.
prove.detailed: You prove a claim when tests, measurements, or logical steps leave little reasonable doubt.
prove.zh: 证明；用可核查的证据表明某事为真
prove.example: Prove that salt water freezes at a lower temperature than tap water.

provide.simple: To give something that is needed or useful.
provide.detailed: You provide help, evidence, or materials when you make them available so a task can succeed.
provide.zh: 提供；给出所需要或有用的东西
provide.example: Provide two examples from the text when you answer the long question.

publish.simple: To share finished writing or results so other people can read them.
publish.detailed: You publish work when you make it public in a newsletter, journal, website, or display after it has been checked.
publish.zh: 发表；把完成的文字或结果公开给他人阅读
publish.example: The Year 6 team will publish their creek report in the school newsletter.
publish.basic: Share the finished writing with others.

record.simple: To write or save information so it is not forgotten.
record.detailed: You record data when you note numbers, times, or observations in a table or log that can be checked later.
record.zh: 记录；把信息写下来或保存下来
record.example: Record the water temperature every hour in the same column of the table.

reduce.simple: To make something smaller in size, number, or strength.
reduce.detailed: You reduce waste, risk, or an amount when you cut it down on purpose so there is less than before.
reduce.zh: 减少；使数量、体积或强度变小
reduce.example: Reduce the plastic in packed lunches by using a reusable bottle.
reduce.basic: Make there be less of it.

refer.simple: To mention a source or send someone to it for information.
refer.detailed: You refer to a text when you point the reader there; you also refer a question to a person who can help.
refer.zh: 提及；指向某资料或请人查阅
refer.example: Refer to page 12 of the atlas when you name the river system.
refer.basic: Point people to the right page.

refine.simple: To improve something by making small, careful changes.
refine.detailed: You refine a draft, method, or model when you polish details so the result is more exact or elegant.
refine.zh: 改进；通过细致改动使更精确完善
refine.example: Refine the hypothesis after the first trial so it names one clear variable.
refine.basic: Make the wording a bit more exact.

reflect.simple: To think carefully about what happened and what it means.
reflect.detailed: You reflect when you look back on work or behaviour and explain what you learnt, not just what you did.
reflect.zh: 反思；认真回想经过并思考其意义
reflect.example: Reflect on why your first estimate was so far from the measured length.
reflect.basic: Think back about what you learnt.

relate.simple: To show how two things are connected, or to tell what happened.
relate.detailed: You relate ideas when you explain the link between them; you also relate an event when you recount it clearly.
relate.zh: 联系；说明两者如何相关，或讲述经过
relate.example: Relate the drought map to the drop in dam levels on the graph.
relate.basic: Show how the two things go together.

report.simple: To tell what you found or what happened, using facts.
report.detailed: You report results when you present them in an organised way so others can trust what you observed.
report.zh: 报告；如实陈述发现或经过
report.example: Report the unexpected result even if it does not match your prediction.
report.basic: Tell people the facts you found.

research.simple: To look for information from reliable sources before you decide.
research.detailed: You research a question when you search, read, and compare sources so your answer is based on evidence.
research.zh: 研究；从可靠资料中查找并比较信息
research.example: Research two reliable sources before you write about the First Fleet.
research.basic: Look things up before you write.

resolve.simple: To settle a problem or disagreement so it can end fairly.
resolve.detailed: You resolve a conflict when the people involved reach a workable decision, not when the argument is only paused.
resolve.zh: 解决；把问题或分歧公正地了结
resolve.example: The captains meet at lunch to resolve the dispute about the final score.

review.simple: To look over work again so you can check or improve it.
review.detailed: You review notes, a draft, or a performance when you examine it with a purpose, such as finding errors or preparing for a test.
review.zh: 审阅；再看一遍以便检查或改进
review.example: Review your notes the night before the scholarship maths paper.

revise.simple: To change a piece of writing so the ideas and wording are stronger.
revise.detailed: You revise when you rewrite parts of a draft after rereading, not just when you fix a few spelling slips.
revise.zh: 修订；改写内容使想法和措辞更有力
revise.example: Revise the ending of the camp story so the last image matches the opening.
revise.basic: Change the writing to make it stronger.

separate.simple: To take things apart or keep them in different groups.
separate.detailed: You separate mixtures or ideas when you divide them so each part can be studied or used on its own.
separate.zh: 分开；把混在一起的东西拆开或分组
separate.example: Separate the sand from the salt water by filtering, then evaporating.

simplify.simple: To make something easier to understand without losing the main idea.
simplify.detailed: You simplify a sentence, fraction, or explanation when you remove extra difficulty while keeping the meaning true.
simplify.zh: 简化；去掉多余难度但仍保留要点
simplify.example: Simplify the long sentence so a Year 5 reader can follow each step.

solve.simple: To find the answer to a problem by thinking or calculating.
solve.detailed: You solve a question when you use a method that leads to a correct, checkable result.
solve.zh: 解决；通过思考或计算求出答案
solve.example: Solve the worded problem by writing the operation before you calculate.

specify.simple: To say exactly which one, how much, or what kind you mean.
specify.detailed: You specify details when you name precise conditions so nobody has to guess what you intended.
specify.zh: 明确说明；精确指出是哪一个、多少或何种
specify.example: Specify the units in every answer on the science test.

state.simple: To say something clearly and directly as a fact or claim.
state.detailed: You state a view when you put it in plain words at the start, before you explain or prove it.
state.zh: 陈述；清楚直接地说出事实或主张
state.example: State your main claim in the first sentence of the persuasive text.
state.basic: Say the point in a clear way.

support.simple: To back an idea with reasons, help, or evidence.
support.detailed: You support a claim when you give facts or examples that make it stronger and harder to dismiss.
support.zh: 支持；用理由、帮助或证据来支撑
support.example: Support each reason with a fact from the recycling audit.
support.basic: Give reasons that back the idea.

suggest.simple: To offer an idea that other people might use or consider.
suggest.detailed: You suggest a solution or meaning when you put it forward gently, without forcing others to accept it.
suggest.zh: 建议；提出供他人考虑的想法
suggest.example: Suggest one change that would make the canteen queue safer at lunch.
suggest.basic: Offer an idea people could try.

survey.simple: To ask a group the same questions, or to look over an area, to gather facts.
survey.detailed: You survey people or a site when you collect comparable information so you can describe a pattern.
survey.zh: 调查；用同样的问题或观察收集可比较的事实
survey.example: Survey every Year 6 class about how they travel to school.
survey.basic: Ask the same questions to a group.

trace.simple: To follow something back to find where it began or how it moved.
trace.detailed: You trace a route, family, or idea when you follow the path through time or space using clues and sources.
trace.zh: 追溯；顺着线索找出起源或经过
trace.example: Trace the Murray River from the Snowy Mountains to the sea on the atlas.
trace.basic: Follow it back to the start.

transfer.simple: To move something from one place, person, or form to another.
transfer.detailed: Heat, energy, or information can transfer when it leaves one object or setting and arrives in another.
transfer.zh: 转移；从一处、一人或一种形式移到另一处
transfer.example: Heat will transfer from the warm rock into the cooler water around it.
transfer.basic: Move it from one place to another.

verify.simple: To check that a fact or result is correct and can be trusted.
verify.detailed: You verify data when you test it again, or compare it with another source, before you treat it as true.
verify.zh: 核实；检查事实或结果是否正确可信
verify.example: Verify the compass bearing before you mark the creek site on the map.
verify.basic: Check that the fact is right.

acquire.simple: To get a skill, fact, or object through effort or learning.
acquire.detailed: You acquire knowledge when you gain it on purpose, by study, practice, or careful collecting, not by accident alone.
acquire.zh: 获得；通过努力或学习得到技能、知识或物品
acquire.example: You acquire a new spelling pattern only if you practise it in real sentences.
acquire.basic: Get the skill by working at it.

address.simple: To deal with a problem or topic in a direct, useful way.
address.detailed: You address an issue when you turn your attention to it and try to handle it, rather than leaving it unspoken.
address.zh: 处理；正面应对某个问题或议题
address.example: The speech should address the crowding in the bike racks, not only praise the new shed.

advance.simple: To move an idea, plan, or group forward so it makes progress.
advance.detailed: People or causes advance when they go ahead in time, place, or influence, often after effort or a decision.
advance.zh: 推进；使计划、想法或群体向前发展
advance.example: Petitions can advance a local cause if the council agrees to hear them.

advise.simple: To tell someone what you think they should do, based on knowledge.
advise.detailed: You advise when you offer a reasoned recommendation, not just an order or a guess.
advise.zh: 建议；根据所知提出该怎么做
advise.example: The teacher will advise you to show working on every scholarship maths question.
advise.basic: Tell someone a sensible next step.

allocate.simple: To give a share of time, money, or space to a particular use.
allocate.detailed: Leaders allocate resources when they decide how much each group or task will receive.
allocate.zh: 分配；把时间、金钱或空间分给特定用途
allocate.example: The council must allocate funds for both the library and the sports field.
allocate.basic: Decide how to share the money or time.

alter.simple: To change something so it is different from before.
alter.detailed: You alter a method, object, or plan when you make a real change to its form or details.
alter.example: Alter only one variable if you want a fair science test.
alter.basic: Change it so it is not the same.

announce.simple: To tell a group official news in a clear, public way.
announce.detailed: You announce a decision when you make it known to everyone who needs to hear it, often at a set time.
announce.zh: 宣布；向公众清楚告知正式消息
announce.example: The mayor will announce the new park rules at Monday’s assembly.

appreciate.simple: To understand the value of something and feel grateful for it.
appreciate.detailed: You appreciate a person, place, or piece of writing when you notice what makes it worthwhile, not only when you like it lightly.
appreciate.zh: 欣赏；理解其价值并心怀感激
appreciate.example: Good readers appreciate how the last line of the camp story echoes the first.
appreciate.basic: Notice why it matters and feel thankful.

approve.simple: To officially agree that a plan or action may go ahead.
approve.detailed: A person in authority approves something when they judge it acceptable and give permission.
approve.zh: 批准；正式同意某计划可以实行
approve.example: The principal must approve the excursion before notes go home.

assist.simple: To help someone complete a task so the work is easier or safer.
assist.detailed: You assist when you give useful support so another person can succeed more easily or safely.
assist.zh: 协助；帮助别人完成任务
assist.example: Older students assist the Year 5 groups during the library research hour.

attempt.simple: To try to do something, even if you might not succeed yet.
attempt.detailed: You attempt a hard task when you make a genuine effort, then learn from the result.
attempt.zh: 尝试；努力去做，即使未必立刻成功
attempt.example: Attempt every scholarship question, even the last, hardest one.
attempt.basic: Have a go at the hard task.

avoid.simple: To stay away from something that could cause trouble or error.
avoid.detailed: You avoid a mistake or danger when you take care not to meet it, often by planning ahead.
avoid.zh: 避免；躲开可能造成麻烦或错误的事物
avoid.example: Avoid copying the sample sentence word for word in your own paragraph.

capture.simple: To catch a moment, feeling, or image so others can share it.
capture.detailed: Writers capture a scene when their words hold the look, sound, or emotion so a reader feels present.
capture.zh: 捕捉；把瞬间、感受或画面固定下来让人感知
capture.example: The first paragraph should capture the smell of wet gum leaves after rain.
capture.basic: Get the feeling down on the page.

claim.simple: To say that something is true and be ready to support it.
claim.detailed: You claim a point when you state it as your position, knowing a reader may ask for proof.
claim.zh: 声称；提出有待证明的主张
claim.example: Claim that shorter lines at the canteen would reduce wasted lunch time.
claim.basic: Say what you believe is true.

collaborate.simple: To work with other people on the same task and share the effort.
collaborate.detailed: Teams collaborate when each person contributes and the group shapes the result together.
collaborate.zh: 协作；与他人共同完成同一项任务
collaborate.example: Year 6 classes collaborate on one Federation display for the hall.

compile.simple: To gather pieces of information and put them into one organised set.
compile.detailed: You compile notes, data, or a list when you collect items from several places and arrange them as a whole.
compile.zh: 汇编；把分散资料整理成一套
compile.example: Compile the group’s notes into one shared page before you write.
compile.basic: Put all the bits into one list.

concentrate.simple: To give all your attention to one task for a stretch of time.
concentrate.detailed: You concentrate when you shut out distractions so your thinking stays on the work in front of you.
concentrate.zh: 集中注意力；把心思放在一件事上
concentrate.example: Concentrate on the reading paper for the full forty minutes.
concentrate.basic: Keep your mind on the work.

conduct.simple: To carry out a test, survey, or activity in an organised way.
conduct.detailed: You conduct an investigation when you lead the steps, keep them fair, and take responsibility for how it is done.
conduct.zh: 进行；有组织地实施实验、调查或活动
conduct.example: Conduct the dissolving test at the same temperature each time.

convince.simple: To make someone believe that an idea is true or worth doing.
convince.detailed: You convince a reader when your reasons are strong enough to change their mind or remove their doubt.
convince.zh: 使信服；用理由让人相信某想法
convince.example: Use two graphs if you want to convince the panel that the creek is cleaner.

cooperate.simple: To work helpfully with others toward the same goal.
cooperate.detailed: People cooperate when they follow shared rules and help one another instead of competing or blocking the task.
cooperate.zh: 合作；为同一目标互相配合
cooperate.example: Houses cooperate to keep the oval tidy after Friday sport.
cooperate.basic: Help each other get the job done.

coordinate.simple: To organise people or parts so they work together smoothly.
coordinate.detailed: You coordinate a project when you time the jobs, share roles, and keep the pieces from clashing.
coordinate.zh: 协调；安排人员或环节使配合顺利
coordinate.example: Two captains coordinate the stalls so the fete queues stay short.
coordinate.basic: Get the parts working at the same time.

create.simple: To make something new that was not there before.
create.detailed: You create a text, model, or solution when you invent it with purpose, rather than only copying a sample.
create.zh: 创造；做出以前没有的新事物
create.example: Create a labelled diagram that shows how the water cycle works.
create.basic: Make a new thing of your own.

deduce.simple: To work out an answer from clues, even if nobody states it.
deduce.detailed: You deduce a fact when you use evidence and logic to reach a conclusion that is not written in one sentence.
deduce.zh: 推断；根据线索合乎逻辑地得出结论
deduce.example: From the muddy prints, deduce which animal visited the creek overnight.
deduce.basic: Work it out from the clues.

depict.simple: To show a person, place, or event in words or pictures.
depict.detailed: A writer or artist depicts a scene when the details let an audience picture it as if they were there.
depict.zh: 描绘；用文字或图画表现人物、地点或事件
depict.example: The poem should depict the storm without using the word scary.

detect.simple: To notice something that is small, hidden, or just beginning.
detect.detailed: You detect a change when a careful test or observation picks it up before it is obvious to everyone.
detect.zh: 探测；发现细微、隐藏或刚出现的事物
detect.example: The sensor can detect a tiny rise in carbon dioxide in the jar.

differ.simple: To be not the same as something else in an important way.
differ.detailed: Two results differ when a feature such as size, cause, or opinion is not identical and the gap can be described.
differ.zh: 不同；在重要方面与另一事物不一样
differ.example: The two graphs differ in scale, so compare the units before you judge.

discover.simple: To find something that you did not know or see before.
discover.detailed: You discover a fact or object when investigation or chance reveals it, and you can then describe what it is.
discover.zh: 发现；找到以前不知道或未见过的事物
discover.example: The class may discover a pattern if they line the shells up by size.

distribute.simple: To give things out so each person or place gets a share.
distribute.detailed: You distribute goods, papers, or information when you pass them around according to a fair or planned system.
distribute.zh: 分发；按计划把物品或信息发给各人
distribute.example: Volunteers distribute water bottles at the community fun run.
distribute.basic: Give a share to each person.

estimate.simple: To judge an amount closely when you cannot measure it exactly yet.
estimate.detailed: You estimate when you use experience or rounding to give a sensible approximate number, then check later if you can.
estimate.zh: 估算；在无法精确测量时作出合理约数
estimate.example: Estimate the volume of the tank before you calculate it with the formula.

exclude.simple: To leave something out on purpose so it is not part of the group.
exclude.detailed: You exclude an item, person, or idea when you decide it does not belong in the set you are using.
exclude.zh: 排除；有意不把某项列入其中
exclude.example: Exclude any trial where the timer failed, and say why in your report.
exclude.basic: Leave that one out on purpose.

influence.simple: To have an effect on what someone thinks or what happens next.
influence.detailed: A person, law, or event can influence choices when it shapes them without using force.
influence.zh: 影响；使他人想法或后续事情发生变化
influence.example: Newspaper cartoons can influence how voters feel about a new tax.
influence.basic: Have an effect on what people choose.

intend.simple: To mean to do something, or to have a plan in mind.
intend.detailed: You intend an action when you have decided it should happen, even if you have not done it yet.
intend.zh: 打算；心里已有要做某事的计划
intend.example: The narrator did not intend to frighten the younger campers.
intend.basic: Have a plan to do it.

limit.simple: To set a point that something is not allowed to go beyond.
limit.detailed: You limit time, length, or choice when you place a boundary so the amount stays within a range.
limit.zh: 限制；设定不可超过的界限
limit.example: Limit the speech to two minutes so every speaker gets a turn.
limit.basic: Do not let it go past that point.

omit.simple: To leave out a word, fact, or step, sometimes by mistake.
omit.detailed: You omit something when it is missing from the final version, whether you chose to drop it or forgot it.
omit.zh: 省略；漏掉或故意不写某个词、事实或步骤
omit.example: Do not omit the units when you copy the measurements into the table.

oppose.simple: To be against a plan or idea and say why it should not happen.
oppose.detailed: You oppose a proposal when you argue on the other side and try to stop it or change it.
oppose.zh: 反对；不赞成某计划并说明不该实行的理由
oppose.example: Several parents oppose the later start time because buses would miss the new bell.

overcome.simple: To get past a difficulty so it no longer stops you.
overcome.detailed: A character or person overcomes a problem when they face it and find a way through, not when they simply avoid it.
overcome.zh: 克服；战胜困难使其不再阻挡自己
overcome.example: The narrator must overcome her fear of the dark ridge before dawn.

overlook.simple: To miss something important because you did not notice it.
overlook.detailed: You overlook a detail when it is there but your attention slides past it, which can weaken an answer.
overlook.zh: 忽略；因未注意到而漏掉重要之处
overlook.example: Do not overlook the command word compare on the last question.
overlook.basic: Miss it because you did not look carefully.

preserve.simple: To keep something safe so it lasts and is not damaged or lost.
preserve.detailed: Communities preserve places, languages, or artefacts when they protect them for people now and in the future.
preserve.zh: 保护；妥善保存使不被损坏或失传
preserve.example: The museum works to preserve the rock-art photographs in a dark, dry room.
preserve.basic: Keep it safe so it lasts.

prevent.simple: To stop something unwanted from happening in the first place.
prevent.detailed: You prevent harm when you act early enough that the problem never starts, rather than only fixing it later.
prevent.zh: 防止；事先阻止不好的事情发生
prevent.example: A lid will prevent the sample from evaporating overnight.

protect.simple: To keep a person, place, or living thing safe from harm.
protect.detailed: You protect something when you put a barrier, rule, or habit in place so it is less likely to be damaged.
protect.zh: 保护；使免受伤害或破坏
protect.example: Fencing can protect the nesting birds from dogs on the beach.

quote.simple: To use someone’s exact words and show that they are not yours.
quote.detailed: You quote a text when you copy a short stretch word for word and mark it so the reader knows the source.
quote.zh: 引用；原样使用他人的话并标明出处
quote.example: Quote one line from the poem, then explain the image in your own words.

recommend.simple: To say that a choice is a good one and explain why.
recommend.detailed: You recommend a book, method, or action when you advise others to use it because you have reasons.
recommend.zh: 推荐；说明某选择为何值得采纳
recommend.example: Recommend one change to the uniform policy and give two reasons.
recommend.basic: Say which choice you think is best.

recover.simple: To get back to a healthy or normal state after harm or loss.
recover.detailed: A person, habitat, or system recovers when it slowly returns toward the condition it had before damage.
recover.zh: 恢复；在受损或生病之后回到正常状态
recover.example: The wetland may recover if cattle are kept off the banks for a year.

replace.simple: To put a new thing in the place of an old or missing one.
replace.detailed: You replace a part when you take the first one away and use another that can do the same job.
replace.zh: 替换；用新的代替旧的或缺失的
replace.example: Replace the flat battery before you start the second trial.
replace.basic: Put a new one in its place.

restore.simple: To bring something back to the condition it used to have.
restore.detailed: Communities restore a building, creek, or artwork when they repair damage so it is close to its earlier state.
restore.zh: 修复；使恢复到原先的状态
restore.example: Volunteers restore the old school well so visitors can see how it worked.
restore.basic: Fix it so it is like it used to be.

retain.simple: To keep something instead of losing it or giving it away.
retain.detailed: You retain facts, rights, or materials when they stay with you after time has passed.
retain.zh: 保留；继续持有而不失去或放弃
retain.example: A glossary helps you retain the new science words after the test.
retain.basic: Keep it so you do not lose it.

secure.simple: To make something safe, or to succeed in getting what is needed.
secure.detailed: A group can secure a place by locking or guarding it; they can also secure funding or agreement after effort.
secure.zh: 确保安全；或经过努力得到所需之物
secure.example: The rangers secure the nesting area with a temporary fence before holidays.
secure.basic: Make it safe, or manage to get it.

seek.simple: To look for something you need, such as help, facts, or a place.
seek.detailed: You seek an answer when you go after it on purpose, by asking, reading, or searching.
seek.zh: 寻求；有目的地寻找帮助、事实或处所
seek.example: Seek a second source if the first website does not name its author.
seek.basic: Go looking for what you need.

shift.simple: To move something from one place, time, or state to another.
shift.detailed: A load, opinion, or weather pattern can shift when it changes position or direction.
shift.zh: 转移；从一处、一时或一种状态移到另一种
shift.example: The wind can shift the smoke across the oval within minutes.
shift.basic: Move it to a new place.

strengthen.simple: To make an idea, body, or structure more powerful or solid.
strengthen.detailed: You strengthen an argument when you add better evidence; a beam strengthens a bridge when it bears more force.
strengthen.zh: 加强；使论点、身体或结构更有力更牢固
strengthen.example: Strengthen your case with a statistic from the council’s waste report.

supply.simple: To give what is needed, such as food, water, or materials.
supply.detailed: A person or system supplies goods when it provides them regularly so others can use them.
supply.zh: 供应；提供所需的食物、水或材料
supply.example: Tankers supply drinking water to the town when the reservoir is low.
supply.basic: Give people the things they need.

sustain.simple: To keep something going so it does not collapse or run out.
sustain.detailed: A system sustains life or effort when it provides enough support over time, not only for a moment.
sustain.zh: 维持；使某事物持续而不崩溃或耗尽
sustain.example: A healthy reef can sustain a large population of fish if water quality stays high.
sustain.basic: Keep it going for a long time.

target.simple: To aim effort at a particular goal, group, or problem.
target.detailed: You target a weakness when you choose it on purpose and put your work there, rather than spreading effort thinly.
target.zh: 针对；把努力对准特定目标或问题
target.example: Target the questions you usually miss, not the ones you already find easy.
target.basic: Aim your work at that one thing.

translate.simple: To change words from one language into another, keeping the meaning.
translate.detailed: You translate a text when you rewrite it so a new audience can understand the same ideas in their own language.
translate.zh: 翻译；在保持原意的前提下换成另一种语言
translate.example: Translate the chorus into English, then check that the feeling still matches.
translate.basic: Put the words into another language.

unite.simple: To bring people or parts together so they act as one group.
unite.detailed: Communities unite when they join around a shared purpose instead of remaining separate.
unite.zh: 团结；使人们或各部分联合成一体
unite.example: The towns unite to fund a shared bushfire siren after the dry summer.

warn.simple: To tell someone about a danger so they can stay safe.
warn.detailed: You warn an audience when you give a clear signal of risk and what they should do next.
warn.zh: 警告；告知危险以便对方可以避开
warn.example: Signs warn swimmers that the current is strong after heavy rain.

weaken.simple: To make something less strong, clear, or convincing.
weaken.detailed: A leaky reason can weaken an argument; rust or heat can weaken a material so it holds less force.
weaken.zh: 削弱；使力量、清晰度或说服力变弱
weaken.example: A fact that does not match your claim will weaken the whole paragraph.

withdraw.simple: To take something back, or to step away from a place or plan.
withdraw.detailed: A person or group withdraws when they remove support, money, or themselves after being involved.
withdraw.zh: 撤回；收回某物或退出某地、某计划
withdraw.example: The club may withdraw from the Saturday fixture if the oval is flooded.
withdraw.basic: Take it back, or step away.

witness.simple: To see an event happen and be able to say what occurred.
witness.detailed: You witness something when you are present as it takes place, so your account can later be used as evidence.
witness.zh: 目击；亲眼看见事件发生并能陈述经过
witness.example: Many children witness the Anzac march from the footpath each April.
witness.basic: Be there and see it happen.

accept.simple: To agree to take something that is offered, or to agree it is true.
accept.detailed: You accept an idea, apology, or result when you receive it as valid instead of pushing it away.
accept.zh: 接受；同意收下所给之物，或承认某事属实
accept.example: Accept the marker’s feedback, then change the paragraph that lost marks.

adopt.simple: To take up a new idea, rule, or habit and use it as your own.
adopt.detailed: A group adopts a policy when it officially chooses that way of working and begins to follow it.
adopt.zh: 采纳；把新想法、规则或习惯当作自己的来用
adopt.example: The council voted to adopt a ban on single-use cups at sports grounds.
adopt.basic: Start using the new rule as your own.

broaden.simple: To make something wider in range, such as knowledge or choice.
broaden.detailed: You broaden understanding when you add new kinds of examples or views, not just more of the same.
broaden.zh: 拓宽；使知识、选择或范围变得更广
broaden.example: Reading both sides of the Federation debate will broaden your view.
broaden.basic: Make the range of ideas wider.

collapse.simple: To fall down suddenly because the support is not strong enough.
collapse.detailed: A structure or system collapses when it fails all at once, often after hidden weakness or extra load.
collapse.zh: 倒塌；因支撑不足而突然倒下或崩溃
collapse.example: The sand wall will collapse if the tide reaches the undercut base.

comply.simple: To follow a rule or request as you are required to do.
comply.detailed: People comply when they act in line with a law, safety sign, or instruction, even if they did not write it.
comply.zh: 遵守；按规则或要求去做
comply.example: Visitors must comply with the quiet-zone signs in the memorial garden.

conceal.simple: To hide something so other people cannot see or know it.
conceal.detailed: A character conceals a feeling or object when they keep it out of sight on purpose.
conceal.zh: 隐瞒；故意把事物或感受藏起来
conceal.example: The narrator tries to conceal her homesickness behind jokes at camp.

consume.simple: To use up food, fuel, or resources so they are gone.
consume.detailed: Living things consume energy when they take it in; a process consumes materials when it uses them until little remains.
consume.zh: 消耗；把食物、燃料或资源用掉
consume.example: The heater will consume less gas if we seal the gaps around the door.
consume.basic: Use it until it is gone.

contain.simple: To have something inside, or to hold it so it does not spread.
contain.detailed: A container contains a substance when that substance is held within it; a report contains facts when they are included.
contain.zh: 包含；内有某物，或将其控制住不扩散
contain.example: The jar must contain only pond water, with no extra soil from the bank.

declare.simple: To say something officially and publicly so everyone hears it.
declare.detailed: Leaders declare a result, law, or state of affairs when they announce it as settled and official.
declare.zh: 宣布；正式公开说明某事已确定
declare.example: In 1901, the colonies could declare themselves one nation after the vote.
declare.basic: Say it officially for everyone to hear.

decline.simple: To become smaller in number, strength, or quality over time.
decline.detailed: A population, trade, or empire declines when it grows weaker or fewer, not when it suddenly stops.
decline.zh: 下降；数量、力量或品质逐渐减弱
decline.example: Frog numbers decline when the creek banks lose their shade trees.
decline.basic: There are fewer of them than before.

demand.simple: To ask for something firmly, as if it must be given.
demand.detailed: People demand a change when they insist on it because they believe it is their right or a serious need.
demand.zh: 要求；强硬地提出必须得到的事物
demand.example: Residents demand a crossing after three near-misses outside the school.
demand.basic: Ask for it in a very firm way.

deny.simple: To say that something is not true, or to refuse to give it.
deny.detailed: You deny a claim when you reject it as false; a person can also deny someone access or permission.
deny.zh: 否认；说某事不真实，或拒绝给予
deny.example: Do not deny the counter-argument; answer it with a fact.
deny.basic: Say that it is not true.

depend.simple: To need something else in order to work or stay safe.
depend.detailed: One thing depends on another when the first cannot succeed unless the second is present or true.
depend.zh: 依赖；需要另一事物才能运作或安全
depend.example: Wheat crops depend on winter rain in this part of the wheatbelt.
depend.basic: Need that other thing to work.

deserve.simple: To have earned something by what you have done or who you are.
deserve.detailed: A person deserves praise, blame, or a reward when their actions make that outcome fair.
deserve.zh: 应得；因其行为或品质而配得上某结果
deserve.example: Quiet helpers deserve credit for packing the whole camp kitchen.

dismiss.simple: To refuse to take an idea seriously, or to send someone away.
dismiss.detailed: You dismiss a suggestion when you reject it without a fair look; a leader can also dismiss a group from a meeting.
dismiss.zh: 驳回；不予认真考虑，或让人离开
dismiss.example: Do not dismiss the other team’s point until you have tested it.
dismiss.basic: Push the idea aside too quickly.

enable.simple: To make it possible for someone to do something.
enable.detailed: A tool, rule, or person enables an action when it removes a barrier or gives the means to succeed.
enable.zh: 使能够；创造条件让某人做成某事
enable.example: Captioned videos enable more students to follow the science demo.
enable.basic: Make it possible for them to do it.

endure.simple: To last through hardship without giving up.
endure.detailed: A person or thing endures when they remain through pain, weather, or time that would usually break them.
endure.zh: 忍受；在艰苦中坚持而不放弃
endure.example: The walkers endure the last steep ridge in silence, one step at a time.
endure.basic: Keep going through the hard part.

engage.simple: To take a real interest and join in with attention.
engage.detailed: You engage with a text or task when you think actively, ask questions, and stay involved.
engage.zh: 投入；真正产生兴趣并专心参与
engage.example: Good questions help the class engage with a difficult historical source.

ensure.simple: To make certain that something will happen or is true.
ensure.detailed: You ensure a result when you take the steps that leave little chance of failure or error.
ensure.zh: 确保；采取措施使某事必定发生或属实
ensure.example: Number the beakers to ensure nobody mixes the two solutions.

exist.simple: To be real; to be present in the world or in a situation.
exist.detailed: Something exists when it is not only imagined—it can be found, observed, or shown to be there.
exist.zh: 存在；真实地在世界上或某种情况中
exist.example: Fossils prove that these sea creatures did exist in inland Australia.

favour.simple: To support one side, person, or choice more than the others.
favour.detailed: A voter or judge may favour a plan when they prefer it and want it to succeed.
favour.zh: 支持；较偏向某一方、某人或某一选择
favour.example: Most of the class favour a later lunch so sport can finish first.
favour.basic: Like one choice more than the others.

forecast.simple: To say what is likely to happen, using patterns you already know.
forecast.detailed: You forecast weather or results when you use data to predict a future condition, knowing it may still be wrong.
forecast.zh: 预报；根据已有规律预测可能发生的事
forecast.example: The bureau can forecast a cool change two days before it reaches the coast.
forecast.basic: Say what you think will happen next.

found.simple: To start an organisation, town, or institution for the first time.
found.detailed: People found a school, club, or colony when they establish it so it can continue after the opening day.
found.zh: 创立；首次建立起机构、城镇或组织
found.example: The six colonies found a federal parliament after the 1901 vote.
found.basic: They start a new organisation that can last.

grant.simple: To officially give permission, money, or a right.
grant.detailed: An authority grants a request when it allows it after considering the case.
grant.zh: 准予；正式给予许可、资金或权利
grant.example: The council may grant permission for the night market on the foreshore.
grant.basic: Officially say yes and give it.

guide.simple: To show someone the way, or to help them make a good choice.
guide.detailed: You guide a reader or visitor when you lead them step by step so they do not get lost.
guide.zh: 引导；指路或帮助别人作出妥当选择
guide.example: Headings guide the reader through each stage of the inquiry report.

hesitate.simple: To pause because you are unsure or a little afraid.
hesitate.detailed: A person hesitates when they delay a decision or action while they weigh risk, manners, or doubt.
hesitate.zh: 犹豫；因不确定或害怕而停顿
hesitate.example: The youngest camper did hesitate at the creek stones, then stepped across.
hesitate.basic: Stop for a moment because you are unsure.

honour.simple: To show deep respect for a person, promise, or memory.
honour.detailed: Communities honour someone when they treat their name, service, or word as worthy of public respect.
honour.zh: 尊敬；对人或承诺表示郑重敬意
honour.example: The town gathers to honour the volunteers who fought the summer fires.

ignore.simple: To pay no attention to something, even though it is there.
ignore.detailed: You ignore a fact or person when you choose not to notice or respond, which can be unfair or unsafe.
ignore.zh: 忽视；明明存在却故意不予理会
ignore.example: Do not ignore the opposite view if you want a balanced discussion.

increase.simple: To make or become larger in number, size, or strength.
increase.detailed: An amount increases when more is added, or when a process causes growth over time.
increase.zh: 增加；使数量、体积或强度变大
increase.example: We increase the lamp height and watch whether the shadows grow longer.

insist.simple: To keep saying something must happen, and refuse to drop it.
insist.detailed: You insist when you repeat a demand or belief firmly, even after others hesitate or disagree.
insist.zh: 坚持；反复强调某事必须如此，不肯放弃
insist.example: The umpire will insist on a replay if the scoreboard does not match the book.
insist.basic: Keep saying it has to be that way.

inspire.simple: To fill someone with ideas, courage, or the wish to do well.
inspire.detailed: A person, story, or place can inspire others when it sparks new effort or imagination.
inspire.zh: 激励；使人产生想法、勇气或向上的愿望
inspire.example: Her letter from the Antarctic base can inspire the class to finish the science fair.
inspire.basic: Give people a reason to try harder.

invade.simple: To enter a place by force and try to take control of it.
invade.detailed: An army or pest can invade when it crosses a border or habitat and occupies land that was not its own.
invade.zh: 入侵；强行进入并企图控制某地
invade.example: Cane toads invade new creeks when floodwater carries the tadpoles downstream.
invade.basic: Push in and take over the place.

isolate.simple: To keep something apart so it does not mix with the rest.
isolate.detailed: Scientists isolate a sample or variable when they separate it, so they can study it without extra effects.
isolate.zh: 隔离；使单独分开以免与其他部分混合
isolate.example: Isolate the infected seedling so the fungus does not spread along the tray.
isolate.basic: Keep it away from the others.

launch.simple: To start something new in a public, planned way, or to send it off.
launch.detailed: You launch a project, boat, or rocket when you set it going after preparation.
launch.zh: 启动；有计划地公开开始，或把某物发射出去
launch.example: The science club will launch a weather balloon on the oval at recess.
launch.basic: Start it and send it off.

manage.simple: To run a task or group so it stays organised and on track.
manage.detailed: You manage time, people, or materials when you make decisions that keep the work under control.
manage.zh: 管理；有条理地安排任务或群体
manage.example: Manage your time on the exam so the last page is not rushed.

migrate.simple: To move from one region to another, usually for a season or a new home.
migrate.detailed: Birds, people, or animals migrate when they travel a long way and settle, at least for a time, in a different place.
migrate.zh: 迁徙；从一个地区移到另一个地区生活或过季
migrate.example: Many shorebirds migrate from Siberia to Australian mudflats each spring.
migrate.basic: Move to a new place for a while.

occupy.simple: To take and hold a place, or to fill time and space.
occupy.detailed: A group occupies land when it stays there and uses it; a hobby can occupy your afternoon.
occupy.zh: 占据；占有并使用某地，或占满时间空间
occupy.example: The new railway yards occupy the flats that once held market gardens.
occupy.basic: Take the place and stay there.

operate.simple: To make a machine or system work, or to be in working order.
operate.detailed: You operate equipment when you control it correctly; a system operates when its parts function as planned.
operate.zh: 操作；使机器或系统运转，或处于工作状态
operate.example: Only trained students may operate the bench drill in the design room.

permit.simple: To allow something to happen, often by official agreement.
permit.detailed: A rule or person permits an action when they give permission and do not block it.
permit.zh: 允许；常指经正式同意让某事发生
permit.example: The rangers do not permit dogs on the nesting beach in spring.

pollute.simple: To make air, water, or land dirty and harmful.
pollute.detailed: People or industries pollute an environment when they add waste that damages living things.
pollute.zh: 污染；使空气、水或土地变脏并有害
pollute.example: Oil from the slipway can pollute the harbour if it washes off the ramp.
pollute.basic: Make the water or air dirty.

practise.simple: To do a skill many times so you become more accurate and fluent.
practise.detailed: You practise when you repeat a task on purpose, watching for errors, until the skill is reliable.
practise.zh: 练习；反复操练使技能更准确熟练（动词）
practise.example: Practise the long-division steps every night this week before the test.
practise.basic: Do it again and again to get better.

promote.simple: To support an idea so more people notice and take it up.
promote.detailed: A campaign promotes a cause when it spreads the message and tries to increase support or use.
promote.zh: 推广；宣传并推动某想法被更多人接受
promote.example: Student leaders promote SunSmart hats at every outdoor carnival.
promote.basic: Help more people take up the idea.

protest.simple: To show publicly that you disagree with a decision or action.
protest.detailed: People protest when they speak, march, or write to oppose a rule they believe is unfair.
protest.zh: 抗议；公开表示不赞成某决定或行为
protest.example: Families protest the planned freeway that would cut through the wetlands.
protest.basic: Show that you do not agree.

purchase.simple: To buy something by paying money for it.
purchase.detailed: A person or group purchases goods when they exchange money for ownership or use.
purchase.example: The committee will purchase extra shade cloth for the summer fete.
purchase.basic: Pay money and take it home.

pursue.simple: To keep going after a goal, question, or path for a long time.
pursue.detailed: You pursue an interest when you follow it with effort, not only when you try it once.
pursue.zh: 追求；长期持续地朝目标或问题努力
pursue.example: She wants to pursue marine science after she finishes primary school.

react.simple: To change or respond when something else happens first.
react.detailed: Chemicals react when they form new substances; people react when an event causes a feeling or action.
react.zh: 反应；因另一事物先发生而改变或回应
react.example: The metal will react with the vinegar and you should see bubbles.
react.basic: Do something because of what just happened.

recall.simple: To bring a fact or event back into your mind.
recall.detailed: You recall information when you remember it accurately enough to use it in speaking or writing.
recall.zh: 回忆；把事实或经历重新想起来
recall.example: Recall the three states of matter before you start the heat questions.

recycle.simple: To turn used materials into something that can be used again.
recycle.detailed: People recycle paper, glass, or plastic when they collect it so it can be processed into new products instead of rubbish.
recycle.zh: 回收利用；把用过的材料再加工后重新使用
recycle.example: The canteen will recycle every clean aluminium can after the fete.
recycle.basic: Turn old stuff into something usable again.

regard.simple: To think of someone or something in a particular way.
regard.detailed: You regard a person as a leader when that is the view you hold; you also regard a rule when you take it seriously.
regard.zh: 视为；以某种方式看待某人或某事
regard.example: Many historians regard the secret ballot as a key Australian reform.
regard.basic: Think of it in that way.

rely.simple: To trust that someone or something will do what is needed.
rely.detailed: You rely on a tool, person, or fact when your plan will fail if that support is missing.
rely.zh: 依靠；信任某人或某物会起到所需作用
rely.example: Do not rely on one website if the article names no author or date.
rely.basic: Count on it to be there.

remain.simple: To stay in the same place, state, or group after other things change.
remain.detailed: Something remains when it continues to be present or true while the situation around it moves on.
remain.zh: 保持；在其他事物变化后仍然留下或依旧如此
remain.example: Three questions remain after you finish the first page of the paper.

request.simple: To ask for something in a polite or official way.
request.detailed: You request help, permission, or information when you ask clearly, often in writing, rather than demanding.
request.zh: 请求；礼貌或正式地提出要求
request.example: Request an extra source if the library copy of the atlas is already on loan.

resist.simple: To push back against force, pressure, or an unwelcome change.
resist.detailed: People or materials resist when they do not give way easily to attack, temptation, or a new rule.
resist.zh: 抵抗；顶住压力、外力或不愿接受的改变
resist.example: Some towns resist the new highway because it would split the main street.
resist.basic: Push back and do not give in.

respect.simple: To treat a person, place, or rule as worthy of care and fairness.
respect.detailed: You respect someone when your words and actions show that their rights, culture, or feelings matter.
respect.zh: 尊重；把人或规则当作值得认真对待的对象
respect.example: Visitors must respect the request not to climb on the carved stones.
respect.basic: Treat it as important and fair.

restrict.simple: To keep something within a smaller range than it could have.
restrict.detailed: A law or sign can restrict access, speed, or choice so behaviour stays inside set limits.
restrict.zh: 限制；把范围收窄，使不能任意扩大
restrict.example: Dry-season rules restrict campfires in the national park.
restrict.basic: Keep it inside a smaller limit.

satisfy.simple: To meet a need, rule, or standard so it is no longer short.
satisfy.detailed: Work satisfies a criterion when it is complete enough; a meal satisfies hunger when the need is met.
satisfy.zh: 满足；达到需求、规则或标准而不再欠缺
satisfy.example: Two labelled diagrams will satisfy the last criterion on the marking sheet.
satisfy.basic: Give enough to meet the need.
